physics_test.description: Leave-One-Out stress test of EFC Hubble friction channel (α parameter) in growth sector. 7 fσ₈ data points (z=0.02-0.85) + 14 BAO points, N2a mode (rd=147.09, σ₈~N(0.81,0.02)). Three-part robustness validation (N1+N2+T7) complete. 7/7 LOO pass, α stable [-1.11, -0.88], no single data point drives signal. Status: Completed (robust hint). physics_test.name: χ-monotonicity in galaxy cluster radial profiles
physics_test.description: Test whether χ(r) = |∇δT(r)|/T₀ ∝ |dΦ_N/dr| increases monotonically from outskirts to core in galaxy clusters within [0.05, 1.0] R₅₀₀. Uses WL mass profiles (HSC/KiDS/DES) or X-ray hydrostatic profiles (eROSITA ER1) to reconstruct Φ_N(r). Tests cool-core and non-cool-core separately. Kill if ≥30% of gold-sample clusters show robust bumps (surviving bootstrap resampling ≥90%), or if cool-core vs non-cool-core require systematically different χ-forms.
physics_test.data_source: eROSITA ER1 cluster catalog + XMM/Chandra gold subsample for X-ray T(r) profiles. HSC/KiDS/DES cluster WL mass profiles for Φ_N(r) reconstruction. Classification: cool-core vs non-cool-core from X-ray concentration measure.
physics_test.prediction: χ(r) is monotonically increasing (Spearman ρ < -0.8 between r and χ) from 1.0 R₅₀₀ to 0.05 R₅₀₀ in both cool-core and non-cool-core clusters, with ≤1 sign change in dχ/dr after Savitzky-Golay smoothing. If this holds, χ is validated as universal regime index. If it fails, χ-concept dies but grid ontology, dual readout, and ×4800 resolution survive.
physics_test.notes: FIRST DOOR TO RISK. Highest-value kill-test because: (1) data exists now (eROSITA ER1 + WL profiles), (2) independent of WP4 baseline, (3) genuinely risky (cool-core variations could kill it). Kill conditions: Kill A = ≥30% gold sample shows robust bumps. Kill B = CC vs NCC require different χ-forms. Kill C = stacking masks non-monotonicity. Failure modes: inner-core-only fail is salvageable (AGN subregime), broad fail kills single-scalar gating. This test must run BEFORE η(a,k,ρ) fitting or T₀→Λ mapping.
